column2: Ahithophel proposes twelve thousand chosen men and a night pursuit, with himself as the acting first-person leader.
David's weariness and weak hands, confusion, flight of all companions and striking the king alone remain the projected plan, not narrated outcomes.
The returning bride comparison, only one sought life and promised peace for all people remain; only is supported by the exceptive one-man restriction.
The plan is right in Absalom's and all elders' eyes; this assessment is not replaced by the narrator's moral approval.
Hushai too is summoned so that his words may also be heard; the repeated additive force remains in as well and too.
Absalom asks whether to follow Ahithophel's proposal and invites an alternative if not; ordinary human you remains.
Not good this time limits Hushai's rejection to the present counsel rather than condemning all previous advice.
Mighty embittered men, bereaved bear and fierce sow remain, followed by the warrior father and selected transitive lodging clause.
column3: He will not give the people lodging remains provisional; lodging among the people is not substituted without resolving the accusative construction.

column2: Propose For behold, now instead of Even now to retain both gar and idou. Hiding, initial attack and the report of defeat among Absalom's followers remain.
column3: The attack infinitive's inferred subject is David, though the source does not separately name him; its exact initial-falling construction remains open.

column2: Even a lion-hearted warrior's heart utterly melts because all Israel knows David and his men's strength; the emphatic melting is preserved.
Propose For this is the counsel to retain the explanatory hoti. All Israel, Dan to Beersheba, sea-sand multitude and Absalom personally among them remain.
column3: Cognate advising/gathering expressions reinforce the proposal; no extra numerical estimate is supplied.

column2: The party will encamp like dew wherever David is found and leave neither him nor one accompanying man; speaker agency and no-survivor scope remain.
A city refuge prompts all Israel bringing ropes and dragging it to the torrent until no stone remains; the image is not replaced by a realistic siege explanation.
The human preference for Hushai is followed by the narrator's divine command to scatter Ahithophel's good counsel and bring all calamities on Absalom.
Hushai reports both proposals to Zadok and Abiathar using the repeated such-and-such formula without pretending the unit restates their contents.
The urgent warning preserves Araboth, no overnight lodging, quick crossing and the unnamed swallowing subject.
column3: It swallow remains unresolved; no named river, army or enemy is inserted as certain agent.

column2: Jonathan and Ahimaaz wait at Rogel's spring, receive the handmaid's report and carry news because they cannot be seen entering the city.
A young observer reports them to Absalom; the pair flee into a Bahurim house's courtyard pit.
The woman covers the pit and cools grain on it, leaving the matter undiscovered.
column3: Grain is the inherited contextual interpretation of the opaque arafoth, not an independently verified lexical identification; the cooling verb is not silently changed to drying.

column2: The woman's beyond-the-water answer misdirects Absalom's servants, whose search fails and who return to Jerusalem.
After departure, the two emerge and warn David's party to rise and cross quickly because of Ahithophel's counsel.
column3: The commands and concerning you are plural despite David being the named recipient; the whole party is addressed through him.

column2: David and all his people cross the Jordan before morning; the selected escaped-notice formulation remains rather than a simplified headcount assertion.
Ahithophel's rejected counsel, homeward journey, household instructions, suicide, death and burial in his father's tomb remain without added motive beyond the stated sequence.
David reaches Mahanaim while Absalom and all accompanying Israel cross the Jordan, retaining the separate movements.
Amasa replaces Joab in Absalom's army; Jethro the Israelite, Abigail daughter of Nahash and sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah retain all selected relationships.
column3: Ishmaelite and alternative paternal names are not imported from other accounts.

column2: All Israel and Absalom encamp in Gilead; no separate date or troop estimate is supplied.
Ouesbi, Machir and Barzillai retain their fathers and origins; the supplying action continues into verse 28.
Ten beds, double-pile rugs, ten cauldrons, pottery and the full grain/meal/pulse list remain.
column3: The two explicit tens are not deleted, and the two meal terms retain distinct working English labels without a settled culinary study.

column2: Honey, butter, sheep and cattle cheese complete the provisions for the hungry, exhausted and thirsty party.
column3: Cheese interprets opaque sapphoth contextually and remains lexically unresolved; no independent dairy identification is credited.

column2: David musters the accompanying people and appoints both thousand and hundred commanders.
Three equal command divisions retain Joab, brother Abishai and Ittai, followed by David's emphatic intention to accompany them.
Propose For if we flee and For you are worth ten thousand, preserving both causal links in the refusal. Repeated enemy disregard, half dying and city-based aid remain.
column3: Worth supplies the comparative sense of you as ten thousand of us; no literal strength equivalence is inferred.

column2: David accepts what pleases the group and stands beside the gate while hundreds and thousands depart.
The three commanders receive the explicit spare-Absalom order for David, and all people hear it; the public scope is preserved.
David's force faces Israel in Ephraim's forest; the battle's two sides are not conflated by the shared national identity.
Israel's defeat before David's servants and twenty thousand in the great crushing remain without a changed count.
Dispersed fighting and the forest devouring more than the sword preserve the comparison without inventing how each woodland death occurred.
Absalom's mule, great oak, head caught hanging between heaven and earth and departing mule remain.
column3: The source names his head, not his hair; no mechanism based on the earlier haircut is added.

column2: Propose Behold, I have seen instead of I have just seen: idou marks presentation, while just adds a narrower time claim than the perfect itself requires.
Propose Behold before You saw him, retaining Joab's rebuke and unrealized ten silver pieces and belt reward.
column3: Pieces is an English unit placeholder for ten of silver; shekels is explicitly present only in the following man's reply.

column2: Propose For in our hearing to preserve the explanation for refusing even a thousand shekels. The public command to the three leaders continues into verse 13.
column3: Even if construes the man's opening weighing expression hypothetically; the exact elliptical construction remains open.

column2: Propose you yourself will stand opposite me for the future stese. No wrong against his life and nothing escaping the king remain.
column3: The boundary of the recalled command and the inferred me after opposite are editorial; the infinitive's relation to the preceding instruction remains provisional.

column2: Joab's I will begin and refusal to wait precede three darts into Absalom's heart while he remains alive in the oak's heart; the repeated heart image remains.
Ten armour-bearing young men surround, strike and kill Absalom, retaining the final killing after Joab's darts.
Joab's horn ends pursuit of Israel because he spares the people; the statement does not erase his contrary treatment of Absalom.
The singular taking, throwing into chasm/pit and raising a great stone heap remain before Israel's individual flight to tents.
column3: He is contextually Joab, potentially acting through men; the singular is not silently converted to an explicit plural burial party.

column2: The pillar's two opaque taking clauses, King's Valley, no-son statement and Absalom's Hand name remain.
column3: In which he was taken and erected it to take remain unresolved. No son is not harmonized with 14:27 by adding a death of the previously named children.

column2: Ahimaaz requests to run with the good news of the Lord's vindication against enemies; its content is distinguished from news of Absalom.
Joab's refusal of today's good-news role and allowance for another day explicitly rests on the royal son's death.
Cushi is sent to report what he saw and bows before leaving.
column3: The selected Chousi can be read as a name or ethnic designation; inherited Cushi is not treated as proof that he is Hushai the Archite despite related Greek spelling.

column2: Ahimaaz repeats his running request despite Joab's question and statement that no useful good news awaits him in going.
The renewed what-if question, permission, Kechar road and overtaking Cushi remain; the road is not replaced by a reconstructed plain route.
Propose saw, and behold, a man running to retain the presentative; David between two gates and the rooftop watchman's viewpoint remain.
The king infers good news from a lone runner while the man draws nearer; the inference is not narrator certification of welcome news.
There is another man expresses the presentative in the second sighting; the king again predicts good news.
Recognition by running style identifies Ahimaaz, whose goodness grounds the king's expectation of good news.
Peace, prostration, blessing and shut out the men who hated their hand remain the selected difficult report.
column3: The hated-their-hand construction is unresolved; lifted their hand is not imported from another reading, and the record does not claim the inherited wording is idiomatic or settled.

column2: The king asks Absalom's welfare; Ahimaaz reports a great crowd and professes ignorance about what was there.
column3: The sending infinitive and Joab/king's servant/your servant grouping remain syntactically open; the inherited clause takes Joab as sender without adding another messenger's identity.

column2: Turning aside and standing here are commanded and performed; no further dialogue is supplied.
Propose Behold instead of Then at Cushi's arrival. His announcement retains today's divine vindication against all rebels.
The repeated Absalom-welfare question receives an indirect wish that the king's enemies become like the young man; an explicit He is dead is not substituted.
